message.content:
The idea of a “best” movie is highly subjective and depends on what you’re looking for—critical acclaim, audience enjoyment, box‑office success, artistic innovation, or cultural impact. Below are a few films from 2020 that received widespread praise across different metrics, so you can pick the one that aligns most with your taste: | Film | Genre | Notable Accolades / Reception | |------|-------|--------------------------------| | **“Tenet”** | Sci‑Fi Thriller | • 7.4 / 10 on IMDb (over 1 M votes)
• 70 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• Known for its ambitious time‑bending narrative | | **“Soul”** | Animated Drama | • 98 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• 8.5 / 10 on IMDb
• Won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature | | **“The Invisible Man”** | Horror | • 8.0 / 10 on IMDb
• 86 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• Praised for its fresh take on the classic story | | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | Historical Drama | • 8.2 / 10 on IMDb
• 93 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• Strong political relevance and strong ensemble cast | | **“Nomadland”** (released early 2020 in the U.S.) | Drama | • 8.1 / 10 on IMDb
• 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• Won the Academy Award for Best Picture (released in 2021) | ### How to decide which might be “best” for you 1. **Critical Consensus** – Look at Rotten Tomatoes or Metacritic scores. 2. **Audience Score** – IMDb ratings or audience reviews on Rotten Tomatoes. 3. **Genre Preference** – If you love animation, “Soul” is a standout; if you prefer psychological thrillers, “Tenet” might appeal. 4. **Cultural Impact** – “Nomadland” and “The Trial of the Chicago 7” sparked conversations beyond the screen. If you have a specific criterion in mind (e.g., best action, best drama, most innovative), let me know and I can narrow it down further!
